as_told.title: Guidance Technologies closes and Northrop's electrogravitics paper

plain: An inventor named Townsend Brown, who worked on using electric fields to lift or push aircraft, suddenly shut down his company, Guidance Technologies, in the fall of 1967 without explaining why, saying only that he got no results. Michels tells this himself, adding that just three months later the aircraft maker Northrop, which he ties to the financier Floyd Odlum, wrote a 1968 paper saying it was investing in that same kind of research. In one telling he also points to a report in the magazine Aviation Week about the B-2 stealth bomber. He tells it to suggest that Brown's work did not end but went secret.
